answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, seeded at independently trusted nodes; each source’s contribution is capped. If a sybil cluster has small external cut relative to its volume, its low conductance limits the trusted flow entering it. A min-cut transitivity bound therefore constrains the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, regardless of its internal node count. Labels such as wharf, nectar, and pigment do not affect the bound; graph connectivity does.
